'''Chihaya Adachi''' (安達 千波矢, born 26 October 1963) is a Japanese scientist and lecturer specializing in [[organic electronics]] which is a field of [[materials science]]. Adachi is the Director of the Center for Organic Photonics and Electronics Research (OPERA) at [[Kyushu University]],<ref>[http://www.i3-opera.ist.or.jp/?lang=en Center for Organic Photonics and Electronics Research (OPERA)] at [[Kyushu University]].</ref> a large multi-disciplinary team of physicists, chemists, and engineers from both academia and industry.

Adachi is recognized as an innovator in the development of materials for organic light-emitting diodes ([[OLED]]).<ref>[https://www.aip.org/publishing/journal-highlights/breakthrough-oled-technology ”Breakthrough in OLED Technology”], [[American Institute of Physics]] (March 2, 2015).</ref> He has pioneered a new technology known as [[TADF|thermally activated delayed fluorescence]] (TADF).<ref>Diaz, Fernando et al.  [http://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/2050-6120/aa537e/meta “Photophysics of thermally activated delayed fluorescence molecules”], ''[http://iopscience.iop.org/journal/2050-6120 Methods and Applications In Fluorescence]'' (2017).</ref>

In 2015, Adachi co-founded Kyulux in [[Fukuoka|Fukuoka, Japan]], to commercialize hyper-fluorescence TADF emitters, and he is a scientific advisor and ex-officio board member of Kyulux.<ref>[https://www.kyulux.com/company “Kyulux: Materializing the Future of OLEDs”]</ref>  Adachi also serves on [[Elsevier]]'s Organic Electronics Editorial Board.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/organic-electronics/editorial-board|title=Organic Electronics Editorial Board}}</ref>

== Early career ==
Adachi held positions at Ricoh Co., Shinshu University, [[Princeton University]], and at [[Chitose Institute of Science and Technology]]. He became a distinguished professor at [[Kyushu University]] in 2010,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/organic-electronics/editorial-board/chihaya-adachi|title=Chihaya Adachi|website=www.journals.elsevier.com|access-date=2017-06-25}}</ref> and his current posts also include director of Kyushu University's Center for [[Organic photonics|Organic Photonics]] and Electronics Research (OPERA) since 2010.

== Education ==
Adachi obtained the degree of Bachelor of Science from [[Chuo University]] in 1986. He went on to earn his Master of Science degree in [[Kyushu University]] in 1988. Adachi obtained his doctorate in Materials Science and Technology in 1991 from Kyushu University.{{Citation needed|date=October 2022}}

== Research, patents and awards ==
Adachi has had over 515 papers published in the field of organic electronics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cstf.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~adachilab/lab/?page_id=3809|title=Paper list {{!}} Chihaya Adachi lab|website=www.cstf.kyushu-u.ac.jp|access-date=2017-06-26}}</ref> Adachi's lab in [[Kyushu University]] has filed over 180 patents since 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cstf.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~adachilab/lab/?page_id=3815|title=Patents {{!}} Chihaya Adachi lab|website=www.cstf.kyushu-u.ac.jp|language=ja|access-date=2017-06-26}}</ref> Adachi's work and achievements<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=MtnJ5HoAAAAJ|title=Chihaya Adachi - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2017-06-29}}</ref> are regarded as fundamental to scientific understanding of OLED device mechanisms, structures and developments. Specific areas in which the Adachi's work was instrumental include highly efficiency phosphorescence emission, OLED host materials and OLED degradation.

In 2012 Adachi discovered a new class of light emitting materials that utilize thermally activated delayed fluorescence, or TADF.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Uoyama|first1=Hiroki|last2=Goushi|first2=Kenichi|last3=Shizu|first3=Katsuyuki|last4=Nomura|first4=Hiroko|last5=Adachi|first5=Chihaya|date=2012-12-13|title=Highly efficient organic light-emitting diodes from delayed fluorescence|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=492|issue=7428|pages=234–238|doi=10.1038/nature11687|pmid=23235877|issn=0028-0836|hdl=2324/25887|s2cid=4376505 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> Since then his research activities are mainly focused on TADF and Hyperfluorescence OLED emission.

In 2014 the [[Society for Information Display]] awarded Adachi with its 2014 SID Fellow Award that honors individuals who have made a widely recognized and significant contribution to the field of information display.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sid-salutes-the-2014-honors-and-awards-recipients-for-outstanding-achievements--contributions-to-the-display-industry-261126961.html|title=SID Salutes The 2014 Honors And Awards Recipients For Outstanding Achievements & Contributions To The Display Industry|last=(SID)|first=Society for Information Display|website=www.prnewswire.com|language=en|access-date=2017-07-26}}</ref>

In 2007 Adachi's paper "Relaxation of Roll-off Characteristics in Organic Electrophosphorescence diodes" won the Outstanding Poster Paper Award at the 7th International Meeting on Information Display (IMID2007).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.kyushu-u.ac.jp/gcoe/eng/members/member.php?id=41|title=Chihaya ADACHI {{!}} Kyushu University Global COE Program Science for Future Molecular Systems|website=www.chem.kyushu-u.ac.jp|access-date=2017-07-26}}</ref> In July 2016 Adachi was one of the scientists recognized at the Japan Research Front Awards 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.jp/press/release/2016/rf2016/|title=日本がリードする先端研究領域と、その領域で活躍する研究者を発表 － クラリベイト・アナリティクス|last=Analytics|first=Clarivate|website=ip-science.thomsonreuters.jp|language=ja|access-date=2017-07-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170724071029/http://ip-science.thomsonreuters.jp/press/release/2016/rf2016/|archive-date=2017-07-24|url-status=dead}}</ref> The award was organized by the Intellectual Property & Science business of Thomson Reuters. Other awards include the 2003 Funai Foundation for Information Technology FFIT Award, the 2004 distinguished paper award on organic electroluminescence (by the Japan Society of Applied Physics) and the 2004 Nano-Tech Award (IT&Electronics division).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sysu.edu.cn/2012/docs/2016-06/20160628173406060814.pdf|title=Adachi's CV (for a Sun Yat-Sen University lecture)}}</ref>

In the 2007 Adachi received the Commendation for Science and Technology by the Japanese Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology. In 2016 Adachi was awarded with the [[Japan Society of Applied Physics]] Fellow Award.{{Citation needed|date=October 2022}}

In 2019, Adachi became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.

In 2022, Adachi received the 92nd Hattori Hokokai Award and the 38nd Kenjiro Sakurai Memorial Award.

In 2023, Adachi received the prestigious medal of honor with Purple Ribbon from the Japanese government.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kyulux |date=2023-04-28 |title=Kyushu University Professor Chihaya Adachi received the Purple Ribbon Medal |url=https://www.kyulux.com/kyushu-university-professor-chihaya-adachi-received-the-purple-ribbon-medal/ |access-date=2023-08-22 |website=Kyulux |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal ==
* He was born in Nagano and raised in Tokyo.<ref name=KYU>{{cite web|url=https://www.kyushu-u.ac.jp/ja/university/professor/adachi.html|title=九州大学 先生の森 安達 千波矢|publisher=Kyushu University|language=ja|accessdate=2025-12-21}}</ref>
* His given name, Chihaya, comes from "Chihayaburu (千早振る)", the [[Waka (poetry)|waka]] by [[Ariwara no Narihira]] in [[Ogura Hyakunin Isshu|Hyakunin Isshu]].<ref name=KYU></ref>
